summary: Fund

Pabrai Wagons ETF, ticker WAGN, NYSE Arca (it began trading on the NYSE on Feb 9, 2026 ; a June 18, 2026 release announced the move to NYSE Arca). Actively managed, long-only, non-diversified. CUSIP 74316P538.
Manager

Mohnish Pabrai is the sole portfolio manager. The adviser is Dhandho Funds LLC, doing business as Pabrai Wagons Advisors, in West Lake Hills, Texas. The prospectus says the fund depends on him and would have to liquidate without him.
Objective

Long-term capital appreciation: a concentrated portfolio of high-quality businesses bought at a meaningful discount to intrinsic value and held for many years. No geographic or industry limits; up to 100% outside the US, including emerging and frontier markets.
History

Started as the Pabrai Wagons Fund, a mutual fund, on Sep 29, 2023. It converted into the ETF on Feb 6, 2026 (first ETF trade Feb 9) and carries the mutual fund's Institutional Class performance history. The ETF replaced share classes costing 1.25% (retail) and 1.00% (institutional) net.
Fee
0.90% a year, a single flat fee. The adviser pays most operating costs. Brokerage costs, taxes, borrowing interest and acquired-fund fees are excluded. There is no 12b-1 fee and no performance fee.
Size
About $298 million in early November 2026 (the fact sheet shows $313.0 million at its reporting date). Pabrai's firms manage $1.4 billion in total across the private funds and the ETF.
Holdings

20 positions. The top 10 are 67.4% of assets (Oct 31, 2026): Reysas REIT 14.9%, Transocean 9.2%, Warrior Met Coal 7.0%, Edelweiss 5.9%, Gimat 5.8%, Valaris 5.6%, Noble 5.0%, TAV Airports 4.8%, Odfjell Drilling 4.7%, Constellation Software 4.5%. The fund reports zero overlap with the S&P 500.
Sectors

Energy 24.7%, Real Estate 14.9%, Information Technology 14.3%, Financials 13.6%, Industrials 12.3%, Materials 11.4%, Consumer Staples 5.8%, Consumer Discretionary 2.9%, cash 0.2% (Oct 31, 2026). At June 30, 2026 the country split was Turkey 29.7%, US 23.1%, India 13.7%, Switzerland 9.5%, Canada 8.9%, Kazakhstan 4.9%.
Turnover
40% for the year to June 30, 2026 (69.25% the year before).
Shareholders

Held mostly through brokers. As of Oct 7, 2026 record holders over 5%: Charles Schwab 23.81%, National Financial Services 19.32%, Vanguard Brokerage 17.69%, Interactive Brokers 10.12%, Stifel 6.94%, Pershing 5.03%.

p: WAGN is the exchange-traded successor to the Pabrai Wagons Fund. The board approved the reorganization on Nov 18, 2025, and shareholders did not need to vote. It closed around Feb 6, 2026. The stated reasons were reaching more investors, greater tax efficiency from in-kind redemptions, intraday trading, lower expected total expenses and daily holdings transparency. The ETF also dropped the mutual fund's 1.00% fee on shares sold within 90 days.

The 0.90% single fee compares with 1.25% (retail) and 1.00% (institutional) net, and 1.84% and 1.59% gross, at the old mutual fund. On $10,000 the prospectus shows $92 for one year and $1,108 over ten at a 5% assumed return. In the year to June 30, 2025 the adviser had been waiving part of its fee to keep expenses at the cap; in fiscal 2026 the fund's reported expense ratio was 0.94% after a waiver and 1.08% before it, and the net advisory fee was $876,703 after a $253,408 waiver.

Shares are created and redeemed only in blocks of 10,000 by authorized participants, so the price on the exchange can drift away from net asset value (NAV). The prospectus lists that as a risk and says the fund's website carries daily premium and discount data.

The record is short and uneven. The mutual fund lost 13.29% in the year to June 30, 2025, gained 3.98% in calendar 2025 against 17.88% for the S&P 500, and then did sharply better after the ETF launch: 28.90% for the year to June 30, 2026 against 22.32% for the index, and 30.14% for 2026 through Oct 31 against 11.77%.

Even so, since inception on Sep 29, 2023 the fund trails the index: 16.91% a year at Oct 31, 2026 against 21.83%. The June 2026 shareholder report says so directly: the since-inception returns 'continue to trail the S&P 500'. Monthly swings are large (+13.8% in August 2026, then about -8.2% in September).
Market-price returns have run slightly ahead of NAV returns at every reported date (table above), so the shares' premium to NAV is a bit wider than at the start of 2026.

The June 2026 report groups about 78% of the portfolio into six themes: offshore oil services (18%), financial services in India (14%), the 'Mark Leonard complex' of Constellation Software-related companies in Canada and Europe (14%), metallurgical coal in the US (14%), the Reysas group in Turkey (9%) and TAV Airports in Turkey (9%).

By Oct 31, 2026 the top ten were 67.4% of assets. Energy was 24.7%, real estate 14.9% (almost all Reysas REIT), and the fund held nothing in the S&P 500. Since March 31, 2026 the fund added Odfjell Drilling and Odfjell Technology (Norway), and Mongolian Mining dropped out of the holdings list.

Valuation claims come from the sponsor's own investor presentation and are not independently checked. For example: Reysas, over $3 billion of liquidation value against a market value of about $2.1 billion; Transocean, a 2–3x return in the downside case; Warrior Met Coal, a 9% free cash flow yield; Kaspi, worth 2–3x its market cap even if its Turkey expansion fails; Gimat, a Turkish wholesale-club chain with two stores today and 'significant execution risk'.

commentary.h: What Pabrai told shareholders on the calls
p: Aug 20, 2025 call: the fund was about $80 million and would turn profitable for the adviser at about $150 million. He said no fee increase was planned and fees could fall as assets grow. He admitted the fund had badly underperformed the S&P 500 in its first two years and argued many holdings need five years or more to pay off, pointing to Reysas, held since 2019, which showed little return for three or four years. He explained most of the early turnover by launch timing and the sizing of Edelweiss (about 20%) and offshore drillers (about 12%). He expects only two or three new ideas a year. He said trades are allocated on a compliance-approved rotation: the Wagons fund gets priority every fifth day, and the three private funds the other days.

Dec 3, 2025 call: the fund passed $100 million that day, and he announced the ETF conversion. He called Edelweiss the largest position (about 18–19%) with several more subsidiary IPOs planned, described Warrior Met Coal (13–15% of the fund) as one of the lowest-cost seaborne producers, and added Gimat, where his funds own more than 20%. He rejected Penske Automotive as too expensive and listed Toll Brothers, Pulte and Occidental among his lowest-conviction bets. He said mutual fund rules force more positions than he would hold in his private funds, which he does not see as a big penalty.

June 10, 2026 shareholder meeting: mostly detailed holding by holding discussion. He called Constellation Software the best-managed holding and said the Kaspi dividend yield is around 10%. On the offshore drillers (over 19% together) he argued that capital intensity does not make a business bad if bought well below asset value, and that Transocean and Valaris is a 'win-win' deal. TAV Airports was down about 30% in dollars over two years because of engine groundings, Boeing delays and low airport fees, and he stayed bullish. He said he no longer sells just because a stock nears intrinsic value, and has no rule forcing him to trim winners. Fund-level performance, premiums and fees were not discussed in that transcript.
I could not open the Sept 23, 2026 and March 11, 2026 transcripts, so they are not summarized here. The replay pages for those calls show the performance tables used above.

Key man: the fund depends on Pabrai and would have to liquidate without him. Non-diversified and concentrated. Foreign and emerging-market exposure, with Turkey (lira volatility, a large current account deficit, political risk) and India (government influence, family-controlled companies, illiquidity, and tax accruals on capital gains that reduce NAV) both named. Sector emphasis of 25% or more in one sector is permitted. Cash can be large for long periods. ETF-specific risks: few authorized participants, cash redemptions, and the chance of material discounts to NAV.

commentary.h: Conflicts and incentives to know about
p: Pabrai also runs private funds through Dalal Street LLC, which pay him performance fees. The adviser's own filing says this creates an incentive to direct the best ideas to the performance-fee accounts, and that trades are allocated pro rata by procedure. The ETF itself pays no performance fee. Pabrai receives no salary from the adviser; he is part owner and gets distributions based on firm profits, plus pay from Dalal Street.

stake.answer: Almost nothing, in the ETF itself. The fund's Statement of Additional Information (dated Oct 31, 2026) reports Mohnish Pabrai's ownership in the fund as $1–$10,000 as of June 30, 2026. That is the lowest range the form offers. A year earlier, for the mutual fund, it said he did not beneficially own any shares as of June 30, 2025.
points: Where his money is: he indirectly owns about 19% of the adviser (through Dhandho Holdings), which earns the 0.90% fee, and he gets distributions from it. He also earns a salary and performance fees from Dalal Street, which runs the private Pabrai Investment Funds. Those private funds hold many of the same companies, and the fund documents say his funds own more than 20% of Gimat.
The documents do not say how much of his own wealth sits in the private funds, so his total personal exposure to these same stocks cannot be read from the ETF filings.

Neither the website, the FAQ, the investor presentation nor the 2025 and 2026 shareholder reports mention a personal investment amount. The adviser's regulatory brochure says only that the adviser, its employees or related persons 'may hold an interest in the ETF'.
Trustees: none owns any ETF shares, and trustees and officers as a group own under 1% (as of Sep 30, 2026).

good: Distinct portfolio. Several writers say the holdings are hard to replicate: international value, mostly outside the US, with zero overlap with the S&P 500. (Bezek, Seeking Alpha; ETF Central)

Pedigree and process. A manager who describes himself as a student of Warren Buffett, with a stated discipline of buying great businesses cheaply and holding them for a long time. Supporters like the willingness to hold cash and to hold winners. (Binary Tree Analytics, Seeking Alpha; the fund's own materials)

Cheaper and simpler than the old mutual fund. The ETF costs 0.90% against 1.00%–1.25% net before, with better tax efficiency and intraday trading. The adviser's own presentation and the information statement make this case.
Recent results. 28.90% for the year to June 30, 2026 against 22.32% for the S&P 500, and 30.14% for 2026 through October.
Steady inflows. Data sites show net inflows over the last one and three months and assets roughly doubling in 2026 (about $150 million in March to about $300 million).
bad: The fee. At 0.90% the fund costs far more than index funds (VT is 0.06% on ETF Database's comparison page) and more than the 0.69% average ETF Database shows for its segment. Ian Bezek, a former hedge fund analyst writing on Seeking Alpha in June 2026, called the fee relatively high and said it is only justified if the unique portfolio delivers, which he doubted. He rated the fund bearish.
Concentration and key-man risk. 20 positions and the top ten at 67%, with the prospectus saying the fund would liquidate without Pabrai.
Country and sector bets. Nearly 30% in Turkey, large energy and offshore-drilling exposure, and cyclical coal, all of which can fall together. India and Kazakhstan add governance and currency risk.

Track record. It still trails the S&P 500 since inception (16.91% a year against 21.83% at Oct 31, 2026), and the ETF itself is under a year old. Binary Tree Analytics noted the short history and said it would watch risk-adjusted results.

Trading costs. ETF Database lists an average bid-ask spread of 3.22% and a median premium to NAV of 0.47% with a historical maximum of 1.87%. Treat that as one data point; I could not check how current it is. Use limit orders, as the sponsor's own deck advises.
Promotional material. The ETF Central article on the fund reads as sponsor-written and does not list fees; the valuation claims in the investor presentation are the manager's own.
opinions.note: What I could not find: I searched for Reddit, Bogleheads, Morningstar, Barron's and WSJ commentary on the fund and none came back readable, so the views above come from the two Seeking Alpha articles, ETF Central, ETF Database, the adviser's own documents and the SEC filings. The fee criticism is the main theme found; I did not find anyone arguing the 0.90% fee is low.

history.title: History: the Pabrai Wagons Fund (mutual fund), Sep 29, 2023 to Feb 6, 2026
intro: The Pabrai Wagons Fund opened on September 29, 2023 as a mutual fund run by Mohnish Pabrai with the same approach as today's ETF: a concentrated portfolio of a few high-conviction holdings, anywhere in the world. It had two share classes, Retail (WAGNX) and Institutional (WGNIX). Retail carried a 0.25% 12b-1 fee and a 0.10% servicing fee, Institutional the 0.10% servicing fee only, and both charged a 1.00% fee on shares sold within 90 days. The adviser capped expenses at 1.25% (Retail) and 1.00% (Institutional) net; before the cap they were 1.84% and 1.59% in the year to June 2025.

It started small: net assets were $32.4 million at June 30, 2024 and $78.9 million at June 30, 2025 (both classes). Brokerage platforms held nearly all of it; at Sep 30, 2025 Vanguard Brokerage held 52.96% of the Institutional class, Schwab 21.19% and National Financial Services 20.74%. The largest single position was an Indian financial company, Edelweiss, at about 20% of the fund when it was bought.
perfRows: NAV rose from $10.00 to $12.47. Expense ratio after waiver 1.01%.
NAV fell from $12.47 to $10.69. Distributions of $0.15 a share ($0.14 of capital gains). Turnover 69.25%.
A very large swing for a fund with about 20 holdings.
After taxes on distributions 9.92%; after distributions and sale 7.82%.
history.perfNote: In short: a strong first nine months, a deep drawdown in early 2025, and a recovery that still left it well behind the S&P 500 at the end of 2025. On the Aug 20, 2025 call Pabrai said the fund had badly underperformed the index in its first two years, more than he would have expected, and that since early 2025 it had roughly kept pace. He argued many of the holdings take five or more years to pay off, citing Reysas, held since 2019, which went three or four years with little return despite a wide discount.
why: Growth. The fund and adviser said the ETF would reach more investors. Pabrai said the mutual fund would not be profitable for the adviser until about $150 million of assets (he said the fund was about $80 million in August 2025). The documents do not tie the conversion to that number, but it shows why growth mattered.

Tax efficiency. ETFs can meet redemptions by handing over shares instead of selling them, which usually means fewer capital-gains distributions. The mutual fund had paid $0.14 a share in capital gains for the year to June 2025. The fund's FAQ says the ETF also uses tax-loss harvesting.

Lower and simpler cost. One 0.90% fee replaced the 1.25% (Retail) and 1.00% (Institutional) net expense ratios, and the ETF drops the 1.00% short-term redemption fee. The information statement shows $92 a year on $10,000 for the ETF against $127 for Retail and $102 for Institutional, and says the adviser could not recoup earlier fee waivers from the ETF.

Trading and transparency. Intraday trading at market prices, and daily holdings disclosure. The FAQ says Pabrai spent most of a 28-year career running private funds for institutions and the ETF extends the strategy to a broader audience.

What shareholders gave up, which the information statement also lists: the ability to redeem directly at NAV, and brokerage costs and bid-ask spreads when trading. ETF shares can also trade above or below NAV.
how: The Trust's board unanimously approved the reorganization. No shareholder vote was needed.
Pabrai announced it on the quarterly call.
The Retail class closed and was merged into the Institutional class.

Last day to buy or redeem mutual fund shares. Holders without a qualifying brokerage account were cashed out around Feb 2 to 5, which could be taxable (and carried a 10% withholding for direct IRA holders).
The ETF took over the mutual fund's assets, accounting and performance history, intended as a tax-free reorganization.
WAGN began trading on the NYSE. A June 18, 2026 press release announced the transfer to NYSE Arca.
history.after: Since the conversion the record has been much better (28.90% for the year to June 30, 2026 against 22.32% for the index) and assets have roughly doubled to about $300 million. The documents do not say the conversion caused either; the period also coincided with strong gains in his energy and coal holdings.
sources: Combined Information Statement and Prospectus, Dec 29, 2025
